title: One holy catholic church
hook: small c: universal; every tradition says it in its own sense

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Paraclete, the one called to stand beside you. Your line was the comforter comes. Who did you stand beside? Day three hundred six.

Sunday morning, a Methodist church. The congregation stands to say the Apostles' Creed, and they come to a line that makes some visitors blink: I believe in the holy catholic church. Catholic? Aren't we Methodists? Across town, at a Catholic parish, people are saying almost the same words. And at the Orthodox church down the road, they say: one holy catholic and apostolic church. Everyone is saying catholic, and not everyone means the same thing by it. Today's word is small c catholic, and it's bigger than any one church's name.
screen: `METHODISTS SAYING CATHOLIC.` → `EVERYONE SAYS IT.` → `NOT EVERYONE MEANS THE SAME.`

segments.voice: Catholic comes from the Greek katholikos, from kath' holou, according to the whole. Whole, entire, universal. Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, wrote letters on his way to martyrdom in Rome, so tradition says, and in one of them he puts it like this, roughly: wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic church. The whole church, not just one local gathering. Later, Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, explained it to people preparing for baptism. The church is catholic, he said, because it spreads through the whole world; because it teaches the whole faith; because it gathers every kind of person, rulers and ruled, learned and unlearned; and because it heals every kind of sin. A monk named Vincent, of Lérins, gave a test, in Latin: quod ubique, quod semper, quod ab omnibus creditum est. What has been believed everywhere, always, by everyone. So when Christians today say catholic, they mean it in their own sense. Roman Catholics mean the church in communion with the pope, where they believe the fullness of the church is found. Orthodox Christians mean the fullness of faith present in each local church gathered around its bishop. In Protestant usage, it means the universal church of all believers, in every place and time, whatever their denomination. Luther's German catechism even says Christian church, instead of catholic, to make that meaning plain. They differ on what the word points to. But Cyril's reasons still sit under each of them: a church that isn't only for one country, one class, or one kind of person.
screen: `KATH' HOLOU: ACCORDING TO THE WHOLE.` · `IGNATIUS: WHEREVER CHRIST IS.` · `EVERYWHERE, ALWAYS, BY EVERYONE.` · `EACH CHURCH, ITS OWN SENSE.` · then, large: `ONE HOLY CATHOLIC AND APOSTOLIC CHURCH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold your local church in mind. Settle, and breathe. Think of the church nearest you, any church, the one you pass on the way to work or the one you grew up in. Picture its doors, its people on a Sunday. Then widen the picture: that church, and all the others on your street, in your town, in your country, around the world. Every kind of person. If you pray, you can pray for that one local church, and through it, for the whole. If you don't, just hold the picture: one little building, and the whole wide world. The bell holds the time.
Catholic. Small c: from the Greek for according to the whole. Universal: the whole church, everywhere, every kind of person.
Your line: universal. Today, notice the edges of your own circle, and let in one person who's usually outside it. Day three hundred six.

howItsDone: Christians across the churches say "one holy catholic and apostolic church" in the Nicene Creed or "the holy catholic church" in the Apostles' Creed, each understanding the word in their own tradition's sense.

fork.setup: you're Cyril, teaching people about to be baptized in Jerusalem. someone asks: why do we call the church catholic?
options: because it is ruled from one city.
because it spreads through the whole world, teaches the whole faith and gathers every kind of person.
fork.reveal: Cyril gave several reasons: the whole world, the whole faith, every kind of person, healing every kind of sin.

original.note: Greek: universal, from kath' holou, according to the whole.

trapdoor: what you thought: catholic means Roman Catholic.
what it means: small c, universal. every church that says the creed says it, each in its own sense.
what a scholar hears: kath' holou; Ignatius's letter to the Smyrnaeans; and Vincent of Lérins's everywhere, always, by all.
